admin.aboveZero: Use a value greater than zero.
admin.areaExplains: An area is where work is filed. Declaring one here is what stops two spellings of the same name becoming two areas that never meet.
admin.areaFolds: Becomes a lowercase identifier, without accents and with hyphens in place of spaces.
admin.areaHint: An area is where work is filed: an agent belongs to one, a ceiling governs one, a policy reaches a set of them and a grant is held in one. Undeclared, every screen invents its own from whatever exists.
admin.areaIdFixed: The identifier is fixed. Saving changes only the displayed name.
admin.areasRule: An area can be withdrawn from new work, but recorded runs still name it.
admin.areasSubtitle: Declared areas are the places agents, budgets, policies and grants can name.
admin.assistantEffortHint: How hard it thinks before answering. Organising text into fields does not ask for much; raise it only if the readings come back shallow.
admin.authoringHint: The model that conducts the interview and writes the read-back when an agent is created. It is not the provider agents use to run: this one never touches a customer system, it only produces text a person approves.
admin.ceilingApplies: Applies from the next run; one already stopped resumes when there is room.
admin.ceilingsInherit: Ceilings inherit downwards and never widen: an area cannot raise what its company allows. Reaching one pauses the run and it continues from where it stopped, rather than ending.
admin.companyFixed: A company is created at installation, not here.
admin.connectFirst: The assistant points at a provider already connected under Integrations. Connect one there first — the credential lives in a single place.
admin.editAreaExplains: The company and identifier stay fixed. Change the displayed name people read.
admin.effectDestructive: Erases or replaces in a way that is hard to undo.

effectHint.destructive: Deletes or overwrites in a way that is hard to undo.
effectHint.write: Changes something, and it can be reversed.

admin.eventsHint: Every configuration change appears here with who made it and when: classifying a tool, registering a provider, removing a server.
admin.currencyHistoryWarning: Changing the installation currency changes how historical costs, ceilings and configured rates are read. It does not convert numbers already stored.
admin.inCurrency: In the installation currency. Leave empty not to cap by amount.
admin.name: Name
admin.noCeilingHint: With no scope ceiling, the only limit is what each agent specification sets per run — nobody can cap an area. Reaching a ceiling pauses the run and it continues later.
admin.noAvailableSections: No administration section is available to this account.
admin.noAreasFoundHint: Try the area name, identifier or company.
admin.marketDefaultChecked: Reference only in {{currency}}, checked {{date}}. It does not count toward ceilings until you save a custom rate.
admin.marketRateOverrideHint: The bundled market default is a USD reference. Enter this installation's own currency before saving a custom rate.
admin.noPricesHint: Known models show bundled market defaults as references. Money accounting still needs a custom rate in the installation's currency.
admin.rateApplies: Applies to runs started after workers refresh their price table. What is already in the ledger keeps the money it was recorded with.
admin.rateLine: in {{input}} · out {{output}} · cache read {{cacheRead}} · cache write {{cacheWrite}}
admin.ratesAreYours: Market defaults are bundled with the release as references only. Add or edit a custom rate to make costs count in this installation's currency.
admin.readMarksRun: A read marks the run. A write after that stops for a person to decide.
admin.reasonPlaceholder: records an internal note on the CRM
admin.recordedInTrail: Recorded in your name in the administrative trail. Correcting it later creates a new record; no record is erased.
admin.removeCeiling: Runs in that scope become bounded only by each agent's per-run ceiling. It is recorded in the trail.
admin.removeRateHint: Runs on this model use the bundled market default when one exists; otherwise they keep recording tokens without money. What is already in the ledger does not change.
admin.sayCompany: Say which company the area belongs to.
admin.sayScope: Say what this ceiling applies to.
admin.subtitle: What the platform talks to, what each tool does to the world, and who changed what.
admin.toolsEmptyHint: Tools appear here when a worker connects to an MCP server configured below and publishes what it found.
admin.undoTakesTheResult: The undo is called with what this tool returned. Leave it empty if an act by this tool cannot be taken back by machine — abandoning a run will say so rather than hide it.
admin.whatItDoes: What this tool does to the world
admin.withdrawArea: It stops being offered for new work. The agents, ceilings and policies already filed under it keep pointing at it and keep applying — withdrawing an area and rewriting the past are different acts.
admin.arriveUnclassified: tools arrive unclassified and are refused until ruled
admin.waitingForARuling_one: {{count}} tool is refused until somebody rules on it
admin.waitingForARuling_other: {{count}} tools are refused until somebody rules on them
admin.nothingWaitingHint: Every tool this installation brought in has been ruled on. New ones appear here when a server offers them, and when one changes under a ruling somebody made.

agents.agentDoesNotHold: This agent does not have it enabled:
agents.alsoGranted: {{tool}} was added to this agent's pack.
agents.areaIsUnit: The area is the unit of cost and of policy.
agents.blockPlaceholder: Write it in your own words…
agents.budgetNeeded: A run needs at least a cost or a step ceiling: it is what makes it finite, and ending is structural here, never something asked for in the prompt.
agents.callerAlsoNeeds: The caller also has to send an
agents.catalogueIsTheOrgs: The catalogue is the organisation's. Here you choose what this agent may invoke.
agents.configureNow: Configure the calling system now. This is the only time it is shown — the platform keeps only its digest.
agents.deniesWhatTheTextPromises: already denies what the text promises:
agents.dragToReorder: Drag a card to change the order. Drop a tool to create a step.
agents.emptyCanvas: No stages yet. Ask the assistant to read the instructions, or write the first one.
agents.emptyCatalogue: No tool in the catalogue. An MCP server has to be connected before an agent can do anything at all.
agents.emptyHint: Agents appear here when a worker publishes the definitions it loaded. Each publication creates a new version; the previous one stays readable.
agents.flowClean: No data from outside reaches a tool that acts on the world.
agents.flowHint: Click a card to edit it beside. The order is changed in Text.
agents.flowPath: {{from}} brings data from outside and {{to}} acts on it
agents.forbiddingTwiceAges: Forbidding in prose what the platform already blocks changes nothing and ages badly: the day the policy changes, the text starts lying. Keeping it only makes sense if the sentence is there to explain the rule to whoever reads the definition next.
agents.hintDefinition: Who the agent is and what it should do.
agents.hintGovernance: Who fires it, how far it goes, and the reading you approve.
agents.hintSteps: The same sequence, as text or as a flow — your choice.
agents.hintTools: The catalogue is the organisation's; this is what this agent may invoke.
agents.idempotencyExplains: The caller also has to send an Idempotency-Key unique per delivery, repeating the same value on every retry of that delivery. Without it, a redelivery opens a second run.
agents.inputPlaceholder: the ticket, the message, the payload
agents.instructionsHint: What the model receives, word for word.
agents.instructionsPlaceholder: You handle tickets arriving at support@…
agents.keptOutsideTrail: Kept outside the trail, like all content: a ticket routinely carries personal data and the trail is held for years.
agents.ladderAlreadyDenies: The platform already denies it, by effect:
agents.ladderDeniesInStrip: The platform already denies it, by effect:
agents.manualOnly: No trigger. This agent only runs when somebody presses the button.
agents.noEventsHint: An agent that declares emits publishes the event when one of its runs finishes, and another that declares an event trigger starts from it. Neither names the other.
agents.noFixedStepsHint: The run chooses its path from the capability pack. Open a run to read the trail it actually took.
agents.noMatch: No agent with that name, in that area and in that state.
agents.noStepsMeans: No steps declared: the run has one envelope, holding the whole pack from start to finish.
agents.noTools: No tool. This agent cannot touch anything outside the model.
agents.noTriggers: Nothing. This agent only runs when somebody opens it here.
agents.notEnabledInStrip: is not enabled on this agent:
agents.notHereNotInvokable: What is not here cannot be invoked, whatever the instructions ask for.
agents.notInThePack: The pack a run is offered is what the agent has enabled. A tool outside it cannot even be proposed by the model: the sentence describes a step that does not happen, and the trail afterwards does not say why.
agents.notInThePackYet: not in this agent's pack yet
agents.nothingChanged: Nothing changed. Publishing now would return the version that already exists: the version is the digest of the content, and the same text is the same version.
agents.nothingToGate: Nothing for the Gate to decide: this stage calls no tool.
agents.packEmptyForStep: The agent has no tools in its pack yet.
agents.pausedOnCreate: A new agent is created paused. Publishing writes the definition; starting is a separate decision, and all four ways of opening a run obey it.
agents.pausedStartWhenReady: The agent is paused. Start it when you want it to run.
agents.payloadIsThis: This is exactly what leaves for the model. Labels become plain lines; nothing is added.
agents.pickAStep: Pick a card to edit, or drag something from the pack in.
agents.proseUnchanged: The prose has not changed since the published version.
agents.publishWritesVersion: Publishing writes a new version. Runs already made stay pinned to the version that ran in them.
agents.publishedWithout: This version was published with no instructions.
agents.reachesNothing: reaches no tool — the agent thinking
agents.readAgainExplains: This replaces the {{count}} drawn steps with a fresh reading of the text. If the text has not changed, you get back the reading you already had — and lose what you arranged by hand.
agents.readTheInstructions: Read the instructions and propose the steps
agents.readingNow: Reading the instructions and laying out the stages…
agents.retireExplains: It leaves the lists and stops running. Nothing is deleted: the versions and the runs stay readable, because a run is only explained by the version it ran under. You can bring it back later.
agents.rightColumnIsPolicy: The right-hand column is what the policy in force will do, not a setting on this agent. Changing it means editing the policy — which has an owner, a reason and a code that appears in the trail.
agents.riskFromOutside_one: 1 brings data from outside, which marks the run.
agents.riskFromOutside_other: {{count}} bring data from outside, which marks the run.
agents.riskNothing: Nothing. With no tools, this agent can only reason.
agents.riskUnclassified_one: 1 unclassified — it will not run until the Curator rules on it.
agents.riskUnclassified_other: {{count}} unclassified — they will not run until the Curator rules on them.
agents.rotateWarning: The current key stops working immediately. Every system configured with it will start receiving 401 until it is updated with the new one.
agents.runOpensOnPublished: The run opens on the version published now and is recorded in your name. A person still decides any action that requires approval.
agents.runsStayPinned: Runs in flight stay pinned to the version they started on.
agents.runsUnreadable: Could not read this agent's runs.
agents.sameThing: Text and flow are the same thing seen two ways: what you change in one shows in the other.
agents.searchTools: Search a tool, or what it does
agents.startFromHint: Four recurring cases. You adjust the text and choose the tools below — a template brings none, because which ones exist here is the Curator's decision.
agents.stepsHint: A reading of the instructions, in stages. The instructions stay the text; this is what the Gate should obey at each moment.
agents.stepsProposedHint: Check and correct them: what stays here is what counts. Tools outside the pack were dropped.
agents.subtitle: Every published version is immutable: the identifier is the digest of the content, so the text a run executed can always be read back.
agents.textAlreadyPublished: This text was already the published version.
agents.textHint: Write the sequence as sentences. Drag by the grip to reorder.
agents.triggerChannelExplains: Starts when somebody mentions the channel bot in a conversation of this agent's area, then starts the message with this agent's id or name. Which conversations those are is decided in Integrations.

triggerNeeds.cron: With no expression this trigger never fires.
triggerNeeds.webhook: With no path this trigger never fires.
triggerNeeds.event: With no event name this trigger never fires.

agents.triggersHint: What starts a run without anybody asking. It grants nothing: what the agent may do is still the pack and the policies.
agents.undescribed_one: The instructions never mention {{tools}}, which a step may call. The agent is allowed something nobody wrote down.
agents.undescribed_other: The instructions never mention {{tools}}, which the steps may call. The agent is allowed something nobody wrote down.
agents.waitingAndLastRun: {{count}} waiting on a person · last run {{when}}
agents.writeFirst: Write the instructions first. The stages are a reading of them — with no text there is nothing to read.
agents.zeroIsNoCeiling: Zero means no ceiling, which is not the same as a ceiling of zero.

approvals.emptyHint: When an agent proposes an action that needs a human decision, it appears here with the reason and what the action does.
approvals.notePlaceholder: Stays in the trail alongside the decision
approvals.subtitle: Steps where an agent stopped because a person has to decide. The decision stays in the trail, with whoever made it.
approvals.willRunNamed: The tool {{tool}} will run, and the effect will be recorded on the trail in your name.

audit.emptyHint: The Gate's decisions, the human approvals and every change anybody makes to the rules appear here — classifying a tool, configuring a provider, setting a ceiling.
audit.sealedEntries: <n>{{count}}</n> ledger entries, chained by hash — each one seals the one before it.
audit.subtitle: What the agents did and what people changed in the rules they run under. Both records are append-only; only one is chained.
audit.unsealedEntries: <n>{{count}}</n> from the administrative trail: append-only by grant, not chained.
audit.verifyIsPerRun: Verifying the chain is done per run, in that run's trail.

branding.auditHint: Changing the installation brand is recorded in the administrative trail. Image content stays outside this setting; paste a URL or a small data image.
branding.externalUrlWarning: An external URL will not load in an air-gapped installation and tells that host whenever somebody opens the sign-in screen. Use a data image when that matters.
branding.iconHint: Compact mark for the collapsed sidebar. Leave empty for the built-in mark.
branding.logoHint: Wordmark or logo image for sign-in and the sidebar. Leave empty for the built-in wordmark.
branding.primaryHint: Hex colour used by primary actions and the built-in mark.
branding.title: Installation appearance

channels.bindingUnreadable: Unreadable binding — remove it and bind again
channels.conversationExplains: The conversation receives the runs of the scope you choose, and no others.
channels.conversationIdCannotChange: To point another Slack channel, add a new conversation and remove this one.
channels.explains: A channel is where runs report and, when inbound delivery is configured, where explicit mentions can start an agent.
channels.nameExplains: Names the connection, not the vendor. Conversations refer to it.
channels.needsWatchAgent: Choose the agent watched messages start
channels.needsWatchRunAs: Choose who watched messages run as
channels.needsWatchSource: Give at least one Slack user, bot or app id
channels.appTokenExplains: Slack xapp- token with connections:write. It opens an outbound WebSocket, so Slack does not need a public callback URL for mentions. Approval buttons still use the HTTP interaction path.
channels.httpExplains: Slack calls the public Request URL and every request is checked with the signing secret.
channels.noAvailableConversations: Slack returned no channel. Invite the bot to the channel, reinstall the app after changing scopes, then try again. If you know the channel id, paste it here.
channels.nobodyBound: No account linked. Without one, nobody decides through this channel.
channels.noneHint: Connect a workspace so runs can tell whoever has to decide.
channels.noMatchesHint: Clear the search, or route an event to a new conversation.
channels.onlyWhereInvited: Only channels the bot has already been invited to.
channels.scopeGoverns: The scope governs: only its runs reach this conversation.
channels.seenAccountsHint: Click an account to fill the link form. It grants nothing until you choose a person and save.
channels.signingSecretExplains: Used only for Slack HTTP callbacks and interaction buttons. Omit to keep the stored one.
channels.socketExplains: A worker connects to Slack from inside the installation. Use this when FuseOne is not publicly reachable.
channels.tokenSealed: Sealed by the vault. Never handed back to a browser.
channels.tokenStored: Stored — leave empty to keep it
channels.wantsExplains: A channel that hears every run finish is one people mute.
channels.modeMentionsExplains: A person mentions the bot and starts the message with the agent id or name.
channels.threadContextExplains: When the mention is a reply, pass earlier Slack thread messages to the agent as untrusted input. This can include messages written by other people, and they may be sent to the configured model provider. Requires the app's history scope for that channel type.
channels.modeWatchExplains: Only messages from the configured Slack sources start the configured agent. The message is still untrusted input.
channels.modeBothExplains: People can mention the bot, and configured Slack sources can also start the configured agent. Each path keeps its own authority.
channels.noWatchAgents: No agent in this scope declares the Conversation trigger. Publish one with Governance → Triggers → Conversation.
channels.watchAgentExplains: The Slack text never chooses the agent.
channels.watchRunAsExplains: This principal authorizes the automated run and supplies personal credentials when a tool needs them.
channels.watchRunAsSelfOnly: You can run watched messages as yourself. Identity administrators can delegate to somebody else.
channels.watchSourcesExplains: One Slack user id, bot id or app id per line. Display names are not stable enough to grant automation.
channels.workspaceExplains: Where an agent asks a human, and where it reports back. One workspace, many conversations.
channels.noDeciderConsequence: Agents can post here, but nobody can approve from this workspace.

common.loadFailedHint: Check the connection to the server and try again.

companies.editExplains: The identifier stays fixed. Change the displayed name people read.
companies.explains: The identifier is fixed; the name is not. Registering grants you inside it, in the same act.
companies.idNeverChanges: Lowercase, digits and hyphens. It reaches URLs and every scope — it does not change.
companies.idShape: Lowercase letters, digits and hyphens only
companies.noneHint: Register one to separate operations that share neither policy nor budget.
companies.noMatchesHint: Try the name, identifier or status.
companies.subtitle: Companies are the top-level boundary for areas, budgets, policies and grants.
companies.withdrawnStayReadable: Withdrawn companies stop new work but remain readable in old runs.

compensation.abandonHint: A parked run is paused, not over: raising a ceiling continues it from where it stopped. Ending it says it will not continue.
compensation.abandonedAsIs: The world was left as it was. Nothing was undone.
compensation.abandonedUndoing: A worker is undoing what it left. Each step lands on the trail.
compensation.failed: The run could not be ended.
compensation.nothingStanding: This run left nothing to undo.
compensation.undoItHint: Every undo crosses the Gate and is recorded. Turning this off ends the run and leaves the world as it is — sometimes that is right, and it is recorded as the choice it was.
compensation.whyPlaceholder: duplicate charge, the customer was already helped by phone

correction.explains: Tick what should have been true. What you tick is checked on every future version — which is why it is a choice and not free text.
correction.noteHint: For whoever reads it in a year. It is not what the battery checks.
correction.recordedHint: This case joins the battery from now on.
correction.title: Correct this case

cost.alertApproaching: {{where}} has passed {{threshold}}% of this month's budget
cost.cacheShare: of what went into the model, at a fraction of the price
cost.emptyHint: Cost appears as soon as the first run finishes. If runs have already happened and the figure is zero, the model provider has no price table — the platform counts tokens and refuses to guess at money.
cost.noCapsHint: With no scope ceiling, the only limit is each agent's own per run. Configure one under Administration → Ceilings.
cost.noTokens: No token accounted for in the period.
cost.spentPerDay: Spent per day over the last 14 days
cost.subtitle: Every run has a known cost before anybody decides to scale it. The run is the accounting unit; agent, area and period are cuts of it.

gate.badArgs: The arguments do not match the tool's contract.
gate.duplicate: This call is already in the trail; repeating it would duplicate the effect.
gate.humanCleared: Cleared by a human decision recorded in this run.
gate.outOfPack: The tool is outside the run's capability pack.
gate.overCeiling: The call would exceed the run's ceiling.
gate.policyRequires: The installation's policy requires handling for that kind of effect.
gate.tainted: The arguments derive from untrusted data read at an earlier step.

identity.emptyHint: Until there is one, this installation has exactly one person in it: whoever claimed the setup token. Configure a provider so the team can sign in.
identity.groupsClaimHint: Keycloak and Okta commonly use groups; Entra ID uses roles.
identity.mappingsHelp: Authenticating proves who somebody is; what they may do comes from here. A provider with no mapping lets people in and grants them nothing.
identity.noMapping: No mapping — anyone signing in here receives no access at all.
identity.removeDescription: It stops accepting sign-ins immediately. Sessions already open are unaffected — revoking those is a separate act.
identity.saveFailed: Saved, but not accepting sign-ins yet
identity.secretKept: Leave blank to keep the stored secret.
identity.title: Sign-in and access

integrations.addressFilledByPreset: Choosing a known provider in the Name field fills the address in. Change it only for a proxy or a self-hosted model.
integrations.addressNeeded: This protocol needs an address. Choose a known provider above and it is filled in.
integrations.addressOnlyForProxy: Leave it empty. Fill it in only to point at a proxy.
integrations.clientKnowsIt: the client already knows the address
integrations.commandRuns: Run by the worker, with the arguments below.
integrations.credentialKept: One is already stored. Leave blank to keep it.
integrations.credentialSealed: The credential is sealed the moment it arrives and never comes back through this screen.
integrations.credentialVault: Sealed in the vault; not even this screen can read it back.
integrations.mcpExplains: An MCP server is what gives agents their tools. Everything it offers arrives unclassified and is refused until somebody says what it does.
integrations.neverTried: No worker has tried to connect yet.
integrations.noProviderHint: With no provider no run advances: the agent has nothing to plan with.
integrations.noServerHint: An MCP server is what gives agents their tools. Until there is one, agents can only reason.
integrations.referencedBySpecs: It is what agent definitions reference.
integrations.removeProvider: Runs that depend on this provider stop advancing. It is recorded in the trail.
integrations.removeServer: Agents lose this server's tools at the next worker restart. It is recorded in the trail.
integrations.serverFromFlag: configured outside the console, by flag or environment
integrations.subtitle: Everything the agents reach outside this installation, and whether it is answering.
integrations.tokenHint: Sent as a Bearer header on every request. Held in the vault.
integrations.tokenKept: Leave blank to keep the stored token.
integrations.toolsAppearHint: The tools appear within half a minute, on a worker's next pass.
integrations.transportHint: A local process is code executed inside the worker's container. A remote address is a request — a far smaller thing to hand somebody.
integrations.acceptLocalExecution: This server runs code inside the worker
integrations.acceptLocalExecutionWhy: A local server is a program this installation starts. It runs as the worker, on its filesystem, and reaches whatever the worker reaches — the Gate decides what a tool may do, and decides nothing about what a process may read. Your name is recorded against this.
integrations.acceptLocalExecutionRequired: Accept what a local server is, or reach this one over HTTP instead.

interview.captureHint: Write it as you would explain it to a new person.
interview.closingHint: The sign that the work has finished.
interview.describePlaceholder: Example: when a billing ticket arrives, I read the message, find the customer, check the history, see whether a document is missing, reply with a short summary and never promise a refund without approval.
interview.goesWrongHint: The exception you have seen happen, and the way out you take.
interview.howDoYouKnowItIsDone: How do you know you are done?
interview.missingCount_one: {{count}} part is still empty. You can continue, but the draft starts weaker.
interview.missingCount_other: {{count}} parts are still empty. You can continue, but the draft starts weaker.
interview.mustKnowHint: Where the information comes from: a record, a knowledge base, a history.
interview.neverHint: The thing that would be a serious problem if it happened. Say it your way.
interview.notDecideHint: What you would take to somebody for approval before doing it.
interview.ready: All seven parts have an answer.
interview.reviewHint: The free description starts as the steps draft; adjust anything missing.
interview.stepsHint: In the order you would take them. A step can be just thinking.
interview.subtitle: Start freely. The platform turns that into seven reviewable parts before drafting.
interview.title: New interview
interview.whatGoesWrong: What usually goes wrong? And then what do you do?
interview.whatMustYouKnow: What do you need to know in order to do it?
interview.whatWouldYouNotDecide: What would you not decide on your own?
interview.whenHint: A time of day, an email arriving, a ticket opened.

manual.title: Manual
manual.subtitle: How the platform works, and why it stops what it stops.
manual.noMatches: No manual page matches this search
manual.noMatchesHelp: Try a system name, screen name or problem such as Slack, MCP, cost or Gate.
manual.emptyHelp: The manual ships with the version. An installation with no pages is out of date.

mcp.subtitle: What this server offers, what we brought in, and what each tool may do.
mcp.surfaceIs: Of what this server offers, these are the tools this installation took. Outside the surface a tool is not restricted — it is not here: no agent is told about it and no call reaches it. Bringing one in does not say what it does; that stays the Curator's separate ruling.
mcp.noToolsYet: No tools yet. They appear once a worker has reached this server.
mcp.noSuchServer: No server by that name is configured.
mcp.leavingAffects_one: Leaving this out stops {{agents}}, which still names it.
mcp.leavingAffects_other: Leaving this out stops {{count}} agents that still name it: {{agents}}.
mcp.recipesAre: What this platform has read about servers other people publish. Choosing one fills the form below — none of them is hosted, supported or endorsed here.
mcp.archivedRecipeWarning: This recipe's source marks this server as archived or not current. Treat it as a reference, not the recommended path.
mcp.configFileWarning: This recipe expects a configuration file. Paste the content into the dedicated field; the worker creates a temporary file and passes its path through the configured variable.
mcp.variablesHint: One NAME=value per line. Given to this server's process and to nothing else — it no longer inherits anything from the worker. Kept in the vault, like a token, because the reason a server needs a variable is usually that the variable is a key.
mcp.variablesKept: Variables are already stored. Leave this blank to keep them.
mcp.configFileHint: Paste the file content. It is sealed in the vault; the worker writes a temporary copy with 0600 permissions when it starts this server.
mcp.configFileKept: A configuration file is already stored. Leave this blank to keep it.
mcp.configFileEnvHint: Receives the temporary file path. Empty uses FUSEONE_MCP_CONFIG_FILE.
mcp.configFileEnvInvalid: Use an environment variable name, such as TOOLBOX_CONFIG.
mcp.oauthHint: Manual OAuth grant. Stored in the vault; use it when the remote server expects OAuth and you already have the grant.
mcp.oauthKept: An OAuth grant is already stored. Leave this blank to keep it.
mcp.oauthBearerConflict: Fill either bearer token or OAuth grant, not both.
mcp.remoteCredentialConflict: Fill only one credential shape for this server.
mcp.remoteBearerHint: Stored in the vault and sent as {{header}}: {{prefix}} …
mcp.remoteHeaderHint: Stored in the vault and sent as the {{header}} header.
mcp.remoteHeadersHint: Stored in the vault and sent as these exact headers.
mcp.remoteHeadersIncomplete: Fill every required header, or leave all of them blank.
mcp.dsnHint: Stored in the vault and passed to the local server as {{env}}.
mcp.authUnknownShape: No recipe narrows this server's auth shape. Use bearer or a manual OAuth grant only if that is what this server expects.
mcp.authNoCredential: This recipe says the server does not expect a credential from this connection.
mcp.authShapeUnsupported: This recipe expects {{modes}}. The runtime does not configure that shape through the token field; use a server-side bridge or wait for dedicated support for that mode.
mcp.noBearerFieldForRecipe: This recipe does not use a bearer token field here.
mcp.storedBearerOutsideRecipe: An HTTP credential is stored, but this recipe documents another auth shape. You can remove the stored credential here.
mcp.storedOAuthOutsideRecipe: An OAuth grant is stored, but this recipe documents another auth shape. You can remove the stored grant here.
mcp.personalCredentialsHint: Credentials stored here belong to your signed-in user. A run uses them only when it is acting on your behalf.
mcp.personalCredentialsLocalNote: {{count}} local servers use installation credentials. A local process is already running before a per-user request exists.
mcp.noPersonalCredentialServersHint: Personal credentials attach to remote MCP requests. Connect an HTTP MCP server first.
mcp.personalCredentialScope: This does not classify a tool or grant an agent a capability. It only decides what credential is attached when a run already carries your delegation.
mcp.personalCredentialEmpty: No personal credential stored for you.
mcp.personalCredentialBearer: A personal bearer-style credential is stored.
mcp.personalCredentialOAuth: A personal OAuth grant is stored.
mcp.sharedCredentialHint: If you do not store your own credential, this server uses the installation credential when one exists.
mcp.sharedCredentialFallback: This server has an installation credential; runs without your own credential fall back to it.
mcp.sharedCredentialDiscoveryOnly: This server has an installation credential for connection checks and discovery. Tool calls still require your personal credential.
mcp.sharedCredentialNotFallback: This recipe requires a personal credential for tool calls. The installation credential cannot stand in for you.

mcp.connectDescription: What it offers arrives unclassified and refused until somebody says what it does.
mcp.catalogueDescription: What this installation reaches, and what it knows how to reach. Connecting one discovers its tools; every one arrives unclassified and refused until somebody says what it does.
mcp.railCaveat: None of these is written, hosted or supported here. What this platform ships is what it has read about them — a recipe fills a form and decides nothing.
mcp.catalogueTabHint: known MCP servers — every connection still needs a surface and a ruling
mcp.nothingHereHint: Try the whole catalogue, or connect a server by address — this platform does not have to know about it first.
mcp.nothingAvailableHint: Every recipe this platform knows about is already connected here. Connect a server by address if it is not on this list.

mcp.connectPanelHint: Fill how this server is reached. Connecting discovers what it offers, but every tool still arrives unclassified and refused.
mcp.connectedWithoutRecipe: Server configured in this installation, with no known recipe in the catalogue.
mcp.noPublishedTools: No tools have been published yet. They appear once a worker has reached this server.
mcp.governanceWriteBody: {{count}} exposed tools can change something outside FuseOne; every call still passes through the Gate and policies.
mcp.governanceReadBody: No exposed tool has been ruled as a write. Unknown tools are still refused by the Gate.
mcp.connectedFooter: Surface changes and rulings live on the server page.

narrative.asks: It stops and waits for a person before {{tools}}.
narrative.asksNobody: It stops for nobody: everything it does, it does on its own.
narrative.boundedBoth: It pauses at {{micros}} or {{steps}} steps, and resumes where it stopped.
narrative.boundedCost: It pauses at {{micros}}, and resumes where it stopped.
narrative.boundedSteps: It pauses at {{steps}} steps, and resumes where it stopped.
narrative.hint: Approve this reading, not the form. It is what the platform will do — every sentence comes from the specification and from what the Gate decides today.
narrative.never: It will never be able to use {{tools}} — the policy in force denies it.
narrative.noTools: It reaches no tool at all, so it can only reason.
narrative.startedByEvent: It runs when the {{event}} event happens.
narrative.startedByHand: It only runs when somebody asks here.
narrative.startedByWebhook: It runs when a call arrives at /hooks/{{path}}.
narrative.startedOnSchedule: It runs on its own, on the {{schedule}} schedule.
narrative.title: What I understood
narrative.unbounded: No cost or step ceiling: nothing obliges it to finish.

notFound.hint: The address matches no screen in the console. It may be an old link, or a screen nobody has built yet.
notFound.title: This screen does not exist

overview.noAgents: No agent published. A published definition appears here with the day's activity.
overview.noCeilingConfigured: No scope ceiling configured, so there is no denominator for a percentage. Spent today: {{spent}}.
overview.noDecisions: The Gate decided nothing today. No agent asked to run a tool in the period.
overview.noRunsToday: No run today. Agents are opened by a schedule, a webhook or an event.
overview.subtitle: How the day is going: how much ran, what the Gate decided and what it cost.

people.assertedHere: What {{provider}} grants. Re-derived on every sign-in — to change it, change the group at the provider.
people.assertedHint: Comes from the identity provider and is re-derived on every sign-in. To take it away, change the group there.
people.emptyHint: People appear here after they sign in for the first time through an identity provider.
people.grantedHere: Granted here, directly. It survives the next sign-in.
people.holdsNothing: They cannot do anything yet: grant the roles on this screen.
people.localExplains: An account that signs in with a password, for when no identity provider is configured yet.
people.matrixEmpty: Nothing granted yet — this person signs in and sees an empty console.
people.noMatchesHint: Search by name, email, id, provider, role or scope.
people.noRoleRule: A person with no role can sign in but sees nothing.
people.passwordFloor: A password needs at least 12 characters.
people.providerScopesReadOnly: Scopes from the identity provider cannot be edited here.
people.setPasswordExplains: Gives {{name}} a way in that does not need an identity provider. Sessions already open stay valid.
people.subtitle: Who can reach the console, and what each one is allowed to do in which company.
people.title: People
people.usernameHint: Letters, digits, dot, hyphen and underscore.
people.usernameShape: Use 3 or more characters: letters, digits, dot, hyphen or underscore.

policies.allMustHold: All of them have to hold.
policies.codeAppears: The code appears in the trail and in the message shown to whoever is denied.
policies.editorSubtitle: A rule evaluated at every agent step: scope, condition, and what happens when it matches.
policies.emptyHint: With no rules written, the built-in default applies: a read passes, a write asks for human approval, and a destructive or financial effect is denied. A written policy tightens that default — or opens an exception with somebody's name on it.
policies.enforcingNextStep: Enforcing from the next agent step.
policies.monitorMode: In monitor mode: evaluated, recorded, changing nothing.
policies.mostRestrictiveWins: The order between policies does not change the outcome: the Gate returns the most restrictive decision among all that match. Deny beats escalate, which beats allow.
policies.noCondition: With no condition the rule covers everything its scope reaches.
policies.noneSelectedCoversAll: None selected covers all of them.
policies.nothingToSimulate: No decision recorded in the period, so there is nothing to simulate. That does not say the rule is harmless — it says there was nothing to compare against.
policies.onlyExceptionIsAllow: The only exception is an allow that matched: it is the one thing that loosens the built-in default, and that is what an exception is.
policies.reasonExplains: It appears in the trail and to whoever is stopped. It is the difference between “blocked by {{code}}” and knowing what to do about it.
policies.reasonPlaceholder: replies to customers go out through a reviewed channel
policies.ruleEvaluated: The rule that will be evaluated
policies.scopeReach: What the rule reaches before any condition.
policies.simulationExplains: Runs this rule against decisions already recorded and shows what it would have done, before saving.
policies.subtitle: The rules the Gate evaluates at every agent step. A policy in monitor mode is evaluated, recorded, and changes nothing.
policies.unknownDecisions: <n>{{count}}</n> decisions could not be answered: this rule reads arguments, and refused calls never stored any. The number above is a floor, not a total.
policies.willApplyAfterReload: It applies at the next agent step once the workers reload the set.
policies.willBeMonitored: It will be evaluated at every step its scope covers, recorded in the trail, and will change no decision.

problem.conflict: That does not hold for the current state: {{detail}}
problem.invalid-input: The request could not be accepted: {{detail}}
problem.not-signed-in: Your session has ended. Sign in again.
problem.not-simulated: An agent leaves Draft by being run against occurrences that already happened. Simulate it first.
problem.saved-not-reachable: Saved, but nobody can sign in with it yet: {{detail}}
problem.upstream-busy: The system on the other side is busy: {{detail}} — try again in a moment.
problem.upstream-refused: The system on the other side refused: {{detail}}

retention.eraseExplains: What the runs carried goes. The runs and their trail remain — we do not erase the record that something happened, only the personal data inside it.
retention.explains: This covers content — what a run carried: the message, the ticket, a tool's result. The trail itself is immutable and survives every erasure: the reference and the digest stay, the content they point at goes.
retention.runsHint: {{count}} named. Find them in the audit trail.
retention.savedHint: It takes effect on the next sweep, which runs once a day.
retention.shorteningWarns: Shortening it erases on the next sweep, and there is no way back. The floor is one day.
retention.title: Retention and erasure

runs.argumentsGone: The arguments are no longer available. Retention erases the content; the trail keeps its digest.
runs.ceilingHit: a run ceiling was reached; raising the matching limit resumes from here
runs.changedState: This run changed state in at least one system.
runs.contentGone: The content is no longer available. Retention erases it; the trail keeps its digest.
runs.emptyHint: Runs appear here as soon as an agent is opened by a schedule, a webhook or an event. Widen the period or clear the state filter.
runs.foldSummary: {{count}} routine steps · allowed reads, no state changed
runs.noMatchFor: No run or agent matching "{{query}}". The search respects the period and the state selected.
runs.noToolsCalled: No tool was called in this run.
runs.noWrites: No write was executed in this run.
runs.replayCount: {{reproduced}} of {{decisions}} decisions came out the same
runs.replayHelp: The recorded inputs are fed back through the Gate, under the policy set each step names and the specification version the run was pinned to. Verifying proves the steps were not edited; this proves they were the answer the rules give.
runs.replayTitle: Would the same decisions be made again?
runs.resumeFailed: The run could not be resumed.
runs.resumeHelp: It continues from the exact step it stopped at. Nothing is redone: what already happened is on the trail and does not happen again.
runs.resumedHint: A worker will pick it up from where it stopped.
runs.stoppedByException: Stopped where the author said it would — “{{what}}”. {{outcome}}
runs.storyBudgetExceededCost: The call would spend {{used}} of the {{ceiling}} cost ceiling ({{already}} already used · {{requested}} requested)
runs.storyBudgetExceededSteps: The call would take {{used}} of the {{ceiling}} step ceiling ({{already}} already used · {{requested}} requested)
runs.storyBudgetExceededTokens: The call would reserve {{used}} of the {{ceiling}} token ceiling ({{already}} already used · {{requested}} requested)
runs.storyBudgetExceededToolCalls: The call would take {{used}} of the {{ceiling}} tool-call ceiling ({{already}} already used · {{requested}} requested)
runs.storyBudgetExceededWallClock: The call would take {{used}} of the {{ceiling}} wall-clock ceiling ({{already}} already used · {{requested}} requested)
runs.storyInsisted: the model insisted on a refused call and the run was interrupted
runs.subtitle: Every run is the unit of audit and of cost: what the agent proposed, what the Gate decided and what actually happened.
runs.taintedArguments: The arguments derive from data marked <l>{{labels}}</l> at an earlier step of this run.
runs.verifyExplains: Verifying recomputes the whole chain and says at which step it breaks.
runs.whatChangedPlaceholder: the area's monthly ceiling was raised to R$ 500
runs.finishedByNoToolCall: The model did not propose another tool call, so the run finished.
runs.finishedByNoToolCallStored: The model did not propose another tool call, so the run finished. The closing answer is held in the content store, under retention and erasure.
runs.finishedByNoToolCallWithOutcome: The model did not propose another tool call, so the run finished: {{outcome}}
runs.outcomeStored: The closing answer is held in the content store, under retention and erasure.

simulation.agentReadFailed: The agent state could not be checked
simulation.agentReadFailedHint: Simulation opens real dry runs, so the console must know whether this agent can start before it spends tokens.
simulation.agentRetiredHint: A retired agent cannot open new runs, including simulated ones.
simulation.agentStoppedHint: Start the agent before simulating it. Simulation is dry at the tool layer, but it still spends model tokens and uses the normal run queue.
simulation.checkingAgent: Checking whether this agent can start
simulation.checkingAgentHint: Simulation uses the same opening path as a real run, so a stopped agent cannot be simulated.
simulation.emptyBody: No run was opened under that identifier for {{agent}}. Upload a set of cases to start a simulation.
simulation.noActs: Nothing has been proposed for this case yet.
simulation.reasonBudgetUnreadable: the ceiling could not be read
simulation.reasonNoProgress: kept asking for a blocked action
simulation.reasonSpec: the version could not be resolved
simulation.setHelp: One occurrence per line, each a JSON object — an export of cases that already happened. Every case becomes a real run with one thing missing: the call. The policy decides, the ledger records, the budget reserves, and the tool answers with nothing. No system is touched.
simulation.title: Simulation
simulation.casesHint: One case per line, each a JSON object with what would arrive as the run's input. A single line is a single run — enough to see what an agent does before it does it for real.

stops.startHelp: Every schedule that has been waiting fires again. Check what caused the stop before confirming.
stops.stopHelp: No new run starts — not by schedule, webhook, event, or this console. Runs already in flight are not touched: stopping is not undoing, and a run that has already acted on the world is ended deliberately, with its compensation.
stops.stoppedHint: No new run starts until somebody starts it again.
